Alex Chen: Hey folks — trying to do my first-week task (run tests in the playground ns) but kubectl keeps saying namespace "playground" not found. I think my kubeconfig has multiple contexts. Can someone point me to the right context/SA to use?

Sasha Li: welcome! :wave: first check your current context: `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config view --minify` to see the user attached to that context.

Alex Chen: current-context is `redwood-dev`. `kubectl config view --minify` shows user: `alex@okta` and cluster: `gke-redwood-dev`.

Sasha Li: ok. We usually ask new hires to either get namespace access via a rolebinding to their Okta user or use the team service account for short-lived tokens. For playground you should either:
1) Use the `dev-playground` SA -> create a token and set it as a kubeconfig user, or
2) Ask eng-infra to bind your Okta user to `edit` in `playground`.

Alex Chen: tried `kubectl get ns playground -n playground` and got "namespaces \"playground\" not found" (I think I messed up the flags). Also tried `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n playground` and got "no".

Sasha Li: `kubectl get ns playground` (no -n needed). If `kubectl get ns` doesn't list it maybe the cluster is different. Run `kubectl config get-contexts --no-headers` and paste output?

Alex Chen: paste:```
CURRENT   NAME            CLUSTER         AUTHINFO
*         redwood-dev     gke-redwood-dev alex@okta
          redwood-staging  gke-redwood-stg alex@okta
```

Sasha Li: yep you're on dev cluster which should have playground. Two quick checks: `kubectl get ns` (to list namespaces) and `kubectl auth can-i impersonate serviceaccount -n playground` to see if you can impersonate. If you can’t impersonate, you'll see a forbidden error.

Alex Chen: ran `kubectl auth can-i impersonate serviceaccount -n playground` and got `no`. Then I tried `kubectl --as=system:serviceaccount:playground:dev-sa get pods -n playground` and got `forbidden: User "alex@okta" cannot impersonate serviceaccount "dev-sa"`

Jamie Ortiz: tagging eng-infra. @eng-infra-bot can you open a quick RBAC request to bind Alex (alex@okta) to `edit` in `playground` or allow serviceaccount impersonation? Ticket details: new-hire onboarding access, needs either RoleBinding or SA-token flow.

eng-infra-bot: Created INFRA-3248: "new-hire Alex Chen - playground namespace access". Assignee: @platform-oncall. ETA 2h.

platform-oncall: Hi Alex — I can patch a temporary RoleBinding. Quick question: do you prefer direct user RBAC (RoleBinding alex@okta -> edit) or a service-account token flow? SA flow is a bit more manual but avoids giving cluster-level access to your Okta identity.

Alex Chen: whichever is fastest — I just need to run test job in playground today.

platform-oncall: Ok I applied a namespaced RoleBinding (edit) for alex@okta in `playground`. Try: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n playground` and `kubectl get pods -n playground`.

Alex Chen: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n playground` -> yes now. `kubectl get pods -n playground` -> lists 12 pods. THANKS! :raised_hands:

Sasha Li: Nice. For long-term we usually recommend the SA token approach for CI or automation. If you want to try that later, run:```
# create token for SA (k8s >=1.24)
kubectl create token dev-sa -n playground
# set a kubeconfig user with that token locally
kubectl config set-credentials sa-dev --token="$(kubectl create token dev-sa -n playground)"
kubectl config set-context sa-dev-context --cluster=gke-redwood-dev --user=sa-dev --namespace=playground
kubectl config use-context sa-dev-context
```

Alex Chen: saving these snippets. Do I need to rotate that token?

Sasha Li: tokens created with `kubectl create token` are ephemeral by default (short TTL); for long-lived you need a different approach (K8s projected tokens or our secrets service). For onboarding it's fine to use RoleBinding.

Alex Chen: got it. Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast turnaround :heart:

Jamie Ortiz: tagging in onboarding checklist to mark access granted (ONBOARD-72). :ballot_box_with_check:
